title: Sino-Agri potash-site unpaid-wage protest
reason: Outside the assigned month: the accessible Lao-language RFA report explicitly dates the gathering to 2022-01-30, not January 2021. It also reports about 30 workers (Laotian Times says 35), below the 50-person threshold, and describes a wage dispute with an employer rather than an explicit demand to the Lao state or its policy.
notes: Laotian Times and The China Project describe the same 2022 incident; The China Project cites local press and RFA, so it is not independent corroboration. State firing into the air is not a basis to backdate the episode. A separate RFA report (S003) describes a Feb 22, 2021 Luang Prabang wage protest with about 100 workers; it has a different location and episode and does not establish a January assembly.

title: Koulong village farmland damage and compensation complaint
reason: No qualifying public gathering is documented. The source describes affected families and a complaint filed with a private railway contractor, but no assembly, attendee count, or public demand to the Lao state.
notes: RFA published on 2021-01-29. “Dozens of families” are affected households, not simultaneous participants. This is a substantive grievance lead, not proof that no protest occurred.

title: Junla village farmland compensation dissatisfaction
reason: No qualifying public gathering is documented. An affected landowner and a villager describe inadequate compensation for 18 families; no meeting or attendance count is reported, and one villager says they were not allowed to show dissatisfaction.
notes: The interviews are published in the 2021-01-29 RFA article; treat 18 families as affected households, not protest participants. The specific start of any collective action is unknown.

title: Guestown-Lao cement plant unpaid-wage gathering
reason: Outside January: the reported gathering occurred on 2021-02-22 in Nam Bak district, Luang Prabang province. The stated demand was unpaid wages from a private cement-plant owner, with no explicit demand to the Lao state or its policy documented for the gathering.
notes: RFA reports around 100 workers gathered outside the former owner’s home. In early February, workers filed complaints with labor departments; do not transfer those later contacts to the February 22 assembly as its target or response. RFA’s April and May reports are one source chain, not independent confirmation. Neighboring February 2021 unit owns any further event coding.

title: “If Lao politics was good” online hashtag discussion
reason: Outside January 2021 and online activity only; no physical public gathering or attendance is established.
notes: RFA says the hashtag began online on Oct. 20, 2020 and separately quotes people inside Laos and a user claiming most posters were abroad. That location claim is not verified. Neither tweets nor estimates of tweet volume are protest-participant counts; Thai street protests that inspired the discussion took place in Thailand.

title: Myanmar migrant workers protest in the Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone
reason: Outside the assigned month: RFA dates the protest to the week before its 2021-08-09 report, in August 2021.
notes: The physical event was inside the Golden Triangle SEZ in Bokeo, Laos; RFA reports hundreds of Myanmar workers demanded that Lao and SEZ authorities allow them to return home or provide food/financial aid. It is not a January event, and participants’ origin is not a basis to relocate an event abroad.

title: Free Youth Guard action at Bangkok’s Victory Monument
reason: Outside the assigned geography: the documented gathering took place in Bangkok, Thailand, and addressed Thai state policy.
notes: Thai PBS reports an action by Free Youth Guard using a 112-meter display to demand an end to Criminal Code Section 112; it notes two detentions but gives no attendance count. The iLaw and Mob Data Thailand pages are regional context, not independent confirmation of this specific gathering. No Laos-directed demand or Lao diaspora participation is established.
